research_question: When is a calibrated limit-order-book simulator sufficiently realistic and sufficiently well-identified to support reliable execution-policy conclusions under parameter uncertainty, model misspecification, regime shift and historical transfer?

contributions.C1: Calibration identifiability: can materially different parameter vectors produce statistically similar observable fit?
contributions.C2: Calibration uncertainty: how much uncertainty remains after calibration when several parameter sets are plausible?
contributions.C3: Simulator ensemble uncertainty: how much do execution results vary across plausible calibrated simulators?
contributions.C4: Execution-ranking stability: do pairwise execution conclusions survive plausible simulators, regimes and bounded historical replay?
contributions.C5: Execution-sensitive realism: which realism failures matter for execution conclusions?

status_meaning.ESTABLISHED: The frozen gate for the stated question passed on the registered evidence.
status_meaning.NOT_ESTABLISHED: The analysis ran validly but the gate did not pass; no claim follows (absence of significance is never equivalence).
status_meaning.FAILED: A preregistered criterion was evaluated and failed in the opposite or rejecting direction.
status_meaning.INVALID: Input integrity, execution or binding failed; outcomes beyond the failure are unknown.
status_meaning.NOT_AVAILABLE: Required data, capability or compute was unavailable; nothing was substituted.
status_meaning.INCONCLUSIVE: The registered evidence cannot discriminate (degenerate, ambiguous or underpowered).
status_meaning.EXPLORATORY: Not preregistered, or run after relevant outcomes were inspected; never confirmatory.
status_meaning.ASSUMPTION_DEPENDENT: The conclusion holds under one declared assumption set (for example optimistic fills) but not another.

v05_history.rule: v0.5 protocol, ledger, evidence bundle and sealed runs are read-only historical records. v0.6 imports every v0.5 consumed dataset and calendar period as consumed and never relabels them fresh. v0.5 outcomes (including INVALID, FAILED and EXPLORATORY_POST_HOC) are cited, never regenerated.

reused_artifacts.v05_control_model: results/v05/m3/select/result.json -> selected (calibration-v2 'combined' model), used unchanged as the v0.5 control class; its canonical hash is sealed in the v0.6 calibration design
reused_artifacts.regime_thresholds: results/v05/m6/thresholds/result.json (development-only 5-minute block thresholds), used unchanged; hash sealed in the v0.6 regime design
reused_artifacts.depth_scale_rule: development median top-5 side depth (native) / 1000 lots, the v0.5 M3 rule, so v0.5 and v0.6 simulators share one lot scale

datasets.prior_use: v0.3/v0.4 calibration and v0.5 M2/M3/M4/M6 development
v0.4 validation and v0.5 M2/M3 selection
v0.4 holdout and v0.5 M2/M3/M4/M6 internal holdout; never used in any v0.6 fit or selection
none: absent from the v0.4 registry, the v0.5 ledger, every repository file and git history at the base commit
datasets.selection_rule: next first-of-month period after the last consumed ETH period (2020-08-01); fixed before access; no substitution if unavailable
same venue, different instrument, same unseen day as the fresh ETH holdout; no substitution
reserved for historical execution transfer v2 and H11/H12; not accessed before the policy evaluation lock; no substitution

not_used.bitstamp-btcusd-mbo captures: consumed by v0.5 (registered M1 outcome INVALID); short self-recorded captures of another venue; order-size and identity observables are therefore NOT_AVAILABLE in v0.6 core
not_used.deribit 2026 periods: consumed by v0.3/v0.4 (imported from the v0.5 ledger); different market era; not used

chronology: development (fit) -> selection (choose model, define near-optimal region and ensemble) -> sealed designs -> retrospective (labelled, consumed) -> fresh same-instrument external -> cross-instrument external -> transfer holdout (after the policy evaluation lock)
holdout_rules: Freshness is derived from the append-only ledger, never from a mutable field; consumed data can never become fresh.
A holdout is consumed at its first ledger-recorded access, which precedes the download.
Every analysis that reads a holdout must be sealed (design hash in the ledger) before that holdout's first access.
Holdout data may not influence observables, binning, thresholds, margins, objectives, parameter bounds, model families, ensembles, perturbations, mandates, policies, seeds or gates.
Analyses designed after a holdout was accessed are posthoc: they are labelled EXPLORATORY and use 'evaluate_posthoc'.
Retrospective datasets were inspected by earlier versions: their results are labelled retrospective and are never fresh confirmation.
A failed download after one retry makes every dependent hypothesis NOT_AVAILABLE; no other date or instrument is substituted.

realism.measurement_operator: One operator for history and simulation: 100 ms causal samples of the top 10 displayed levels per side plus aggressor-grouped trade events (the v0.5 grouping rule). Quantities in lots (development depth scale), prices in basis points of mid or ticks. Historical samples older than 5 s are invalid.
realism.sketch: Each 600 s block is reduced to additive sufficient statistics (histograms on development-frozen bins, moment sums for paired statistics, count matrices). Pooling and block resampling add sketches; every distance is computed from pooled sketches.

families.book_state: spread (bps), L1/top-5/top-10 side depth (log lots), side asymmetry log(bid5/ask5), top-5 imbalance, depth concentration L1/top-10, book slope log(top-5/L1), level gaps (ticks, levels 1-5), microprice deviation from mid (bps)
families.event_activity: counts per 10 s (log1p) of aggressive trade events, top-10 book changes, displayed additions and net cancellations; trade interarrival times (log)
families.sizes: aggressive event size, displayed addition size, net cancellation size (log lots); individual order size NOT_AVAILABLE (aggregate L2)
families.returns: mid log returns at 1 s, 10 s and 60 s (bps), 60 s realized volatility (log1p bps), nonzero 1 s return fraction
families.tail: exceedance probabilities at development-frozen thresholds (spread > p99, top-5 depth < p1, 60 s volatility > p99, event size > p99, 10 s cancellation count > p99, |imbalance| > p99, |10 s return| > p99.9) and 1%/99% quantile errors; Hill tail index of event sizes and |10 s returns| only when at least 50 exceedances exist, else NOT_AVAILABLE
families.temporal: lagged autocorrelations (1 s grid) of returns (1, 2, 5, 10), |returns| (1, 5, 10, 30), spread (1, 10), top-5 depth (1, 10, 60), imbalance (1, 10, 60); 10 s grid of signed event volume (1, 2, 5) and event counts (1, 6); partial autocorrelation of returns at lag 2; wide-spread run lengths (log)
families.event_process: 100 ms event-state chain over {quiet, trade, add-only, cancel-only, add-and-cancel}: state proportions, conditional transition rows, P(cancel next | trade), P(trade next | cancel); Fano factors of trade counts at 1 s and 10 s; interarrival burstiness; L1 depletion and replenishment hazards; cross-excitation proxy corr(trade count_t, cancellation count_t+1). Descriptive excitation diagnostics only, never a causal generative claim.
families.dependence: rank correlations on development-frozen marginal scale: (60 s volatility, spread), (volatility, top-5 depth), (event count, volatility), (cancellation count, volatility), (|imbalance|, spread) on 60 s windows; (imbalance_t, return_t+1s), (microprice deviation_t, return_t+1s), (signed event volume_t, return_t), (top-5 depth_t, |return_t+1s|) on the 1 s grid; mean next-second return by development imbalance quintile; mutual information of imbalance quintile and next return sign
families.resilience: time for opposite L1 depth to regain 90% of its pre-event level after an event removing >= 50% of it (log s, 30 s censoring), recovered fraction, wide-spread recovery time (log s), censored fraction

capability_not_available: modify intensity (aggregate L2 cannot separate modifies)

distances.primary: normalized 1-Wasserstein distance on the transformed scale (log for positive heavy-tailed quantities) divided by the development interquartile range with a physical floor (1 tick for spread, returns and microprice; 0.1 log units otherwise)
also_reported: Jensen-Shannon divergence (base 2) on the frozen bins
distances.scalar_components: absolute difference for correlations, autocorrelations and probabilities on the correlation/probability scale; |log ratio| for rates, Fano factors and exceedance probabilities (floor 1e-4)

realism.family_error: mean of the family's evaluable component errors (also reported: max); a component is NOT_EVALUABLE when either side has fewer than its minimum samples (50 distribution samples, 300 paired samples, 30 exceedance-eligible windows)
realism.objective_normalization: development-only scale per family: the family error between the first and second 12 hours of the development day (floor 0.05)
realism.calibration_objective: mean over the nine families of (family error / development scale); this is the preregistered calibration objective, not a validity score
realism.equivalence_margins: per family, the real-versus-real family error between the full development day and the full selection day (both consumed), computed by the sealed observable implementation and sealed in the ledger before any holdout access
realism.scorecard: family-level only; no headline aggregate other than the labelled calibration objective; domain-gap, regime and execution-sensitivity dimensions are reported beside the nine families

calibration.model_family: lob.sim_v2.ExtendedSimulator (unchanged) with all v0.5 extensions available; empirical size tables fixed from development (v0.5 rule)
calibration.parameters: 8 base parameters (target_level_vol, limit_rate, market_rate, cancel_rate, offset_p, limit_qty_mean, market_qty_mean, resilience) and 8 extension parameters (inside_spread_prob, cancel_depth_exponent, imbalance_beta, regime_multiplier, regime_switch_rate, regime_high_share, hawkes branching ratio, hawkes_decay); bounds and transforms sealed in the calibration design from development data only
calibration.search: 8 independent seeded starts; each start: 96 global draws in the transformed box, then 3 refinement rounds of 64 perturbations around the start's incumbent (step scale 0.25, 0.12, 0.06 of the transformed range); 2304 candidates; every candidate evaluated on the same 3 fit seeds x 1800 simulated seconds after 60 s warmup
calibration.rescore: the 64 lowest-objective distinct candidates are re-scored on development with 5 fresh seeds x 3600 s; the 32 best re-scored candidates advance to selection
calibration.selection: the 32 candidates and the v0.5 control are scored on the selection day with 5 selection seeds x 3600 s; the selected v3 model minimizes the selection objective (ties: lower development re-score)
calibration.constraints: none in the primary objective; family-level constraint filtering is reported as a sensitivity
calibration.pareto: the Pareto set over the nine family errors among the 64 re-scored candidates is reported descriptively
calibration.failure: a candidate that raises, hits max_events or yields a non-finite objective gets objective +inf, is retained and counted

identifiability.near_optimal_region: selection-day objective <= min + max(0.10 * min, 2 * SE), SE = between-seed standard error of the selected model's selection objective; fixed from selection data only
identifiability.material_distinctness: L-infinity distance >= 0.25 between parameter vectors in the transformed unit box
identifiability.distinct_set: greedy pass over the near-optimal region in ascending selection objective, keeping a candidate if it is materially distinct from every kept candidate
diagnostics: parameter ranges and correlations within the near-optimal region
local one-at-a-time sensitivity of every family error to +/-10% transformed-range steps around the selected model (development, 3 seeds x 1800 s)
profile diagnostics: each parameter fixed at 5 grid points while the others are re-optimized by 24 perturbation draws
flat directions: eigen-decomposition of the near-optimal parameter covariance and of the local sensitivity Gram matrix
optional Morris elementary effects (12 trajectories), labelled EXPLORATORY

ensemble.members: the distinct near-optimal set (selected model first), at most 8 members
ensemble.single_member_rule: if only one member exists, ensemble-based quantities are NOT_AVAILABLE and only structural perturbation worlds are used

interventions.spread_distortion: offset_p shifted to its lower bound (orders placed further from the touch)
interventions.persistence_removed: hawkes branching ratio and regime switching removed

misspecification.interpretation: synthetic interventions on the simulator only; no causal statement about real markets follows

mandate.quantity_rule: round(development median L1 depth in lots)
mandate.completion: v0.5 completion constraint, urgency fraction 0.8; within-horizon and settlement completion reported separately

agents.excluded: heuristic and random v0.5 controls (not execution strategies of interest) and no new baselines

learned_variants.single: trained on the selected v3 world only
learned_variants.ensemble: trained with one ensemble member drawn uniformly at each episode reset (domain randomization derived from the v0.6 ensemble, not arbitrary ranges)

training.observation: v0.4 observation contract, normalization fitted on training-world random exploration and sealed before fitting

execution.ac_parameters: identified per world on 4 identification seeds with the repository estimator
execution.worlds: selected v3 model, each ensemble member, each structural intervention, the regime-conditioned models and the v0.5 control
execution.market_seeds: 200 evaluation market seeds per world, identical across worlds and agents
execution.environment_freeze: configs/v06/environment-freeze.json written and sealed before any policy training or registered execution evaluation

transfer.replay: lob.historical_sim.HistoricalSimulator (unchanged): identity-free displayed liquidity reset to history, bounded passive fills, no exact FIFO, no market impact of the hypothetical parent
transfer.mapping: clock ratio 1 (v0.6 worlds are calibrated in real seconds); lots per native unit = 1 / development depth scale
transfer.episodes: 144 episodes starting at first capture + 300 s + 600 s * k; window = warmup + horizon + settlement + 1 s; 20 book levels
transfer.classification: per pair and source: predicted direction (Bonferroni interval excludes zero) versus historical direction in each fill mode: agrees, reverses, assumption_dependent, indeterminate, not_evaluable

domain_gap.features: scale-free window statistics only (spreads in bps, depths in development-scaled lots, returns in bps, counts, fractions, correlations); the feature whitelist is sealed in the domain-gap design
domain_gap.split: real windows chronological (first half train, 10-minute purge, second half test); simulated windows grouped by seed (first half of seeds train, second half test); classes balanced by deterministic subsampling

classifiers.primary: L2-regularized logistic regression on training-standardized features

domain_gap.interpretation: a strong discriminator is evidence of a detectable domain gap; a weak discriminator is not evidence of realism

regimes.thresholds: v0.5 M6 development-only 5-minute block thresholds, unchanged
regimes.conditioned_dimension: volatility (high/low median split); one dimension only, fixed before any regime-conditioned fit
regimes.regime_fits: high- and low-volatility development blocks, each with 4 starts of the calibration-v3 search (1152 candidates) and the same rescore/selection pipeline restricted to that regime's blocks
regimes.transition_realism: 5-minute block labels (volatility, spread, activity, stress) on simulated paths of 8 seeds x 6 h: transition matrices, dwell times, stress entry and recovery frequencies, compared with each historical dataset

ood.rule: 60 s window features standardized by development statistics; 5-nearest-neighbour distance from each historical window to the ensemble's simulated windows; threshold = 99th percentile of leave-one-seed-out simulated distances; windows above it are OUT_OF_SUPPORT
ood.no_claim: a dataset with more than 50% of windows out of support is labelled NO_CLAIM for absolute realism statements

H1.question: Does the selected calibration-v3 model reduce the v0.6 calibration objective relative to the v0.5 control on retrospective data?
H1.estimator: objective(v3) - objective(v0.5 control) on the full retrospective day
H1.uncertainty: paired moving-block bootstrap of historical blocks with independent seed-level bootstrap of each model's simulations, 2000 resamples
H1.label: retrospective

H2.question: Does the improvement generalize to a fresh same-instrument period?

H3.question: Does the improvement generalize cross-instrument?
H3.estimator: as H1 with the ETH development scale and tick geometry applied unchanged

H4.question: Do multiple materially distinct parameter vectors remain within the near-optimal calibration region?
H4.estimator: size of the greedy materially-distinct near-optimal set
H4.uncertainty: near-optimal rule includes 2 x between-seed SE; descriptive count
H4.failure_semantics: count = 1: NOT_ESTABLISHED (parameters locally identified at this resolution); search failure: INVALID

H5.question: Do near-optimal parameter sets produce materially different execution outcomes?
H5.estimator: for each classical agent and member pair: difference of mean completion-adjusted cost over the 200 evaluation market seeds
H5.sample_unit: market seeds within each world (independent across worlds)
H5.uncertainty: independent percentile bootstrap of each world's market seeds, 5000 resamples
H5.threshold: some contrast has a Bonferroni interval excluding zero and |difference| >= 1.0 bps (about a quarter of the development tick in bps)
H5.failure_semantics: no such contrast: NOT_ESTABLISHED; fewer than 2 members: NOT_AVAILABLE

H6.question: Are execution rankings non-invariant across plausible simulator configurations?
H6.estimator: per agent pair and ensemble member: paired (same market seeds) mean cost difference
H6.uncertainty: paired percentile bootstrap, 5000 resamples; learned agents averaged over training seeds per market seed
H6.threshold: a certified reversal: some pair has Bonferroni intervals excluding zero in opposite directions in two members
H6.failure_semantics: no certified reversal: NOT_ESTABLISHED (invariance is not thereby established); fewer than 2 members: NOT_AVAILABLE
H6.status_rule: ESTABLISHED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / NOT_AVAILABLE; sign stability, rank correlation, reversal and indeterminate fractions are reported

H7.question: Do specific realism-error families explain substantial variation in execution-conclusion instability across simulator worlds?
H7.estimator: Spearman correlation across worlds (ensemble and structural interventions) between family error on the selection day and the conclusion-disagreement fraction relative to the selected world
H7.threshold: some family has rho >= 0.5 with its Holm-adjusted one-sided interval excluding zero
H7.failure_semantics: otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED; fewer than 8 worlds: INCONCLUSIVE
H7.status_rule: ESTABLISHED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / INCONCLUSIVE; within-simulator association only

H8.question: Are real and synthetic trajectories distinguishable under leakage-resistant two-sample testing?
H8.estimator: test-set ROC-AUC of the primary logistic discriminator (fresh ETH windows versus selected v3 windows)
H8.sample_unit: 60 s windows (block-resampled in blocks of 10 windows; simulated windows by seed)

H9.question: Does regime-conditioned calibration improve within-regime realism?
H9.estimator: per volatility regime: objective(regime model) - objective(global v3) on that regime's 5-minute blocks
H9.uncertainty: paired block bootstrap with seed bootstrap, 2000 resamples
H9.threshold: Bonferroni upper bound < 0 in both regimes
H9.failure_semantics: a regime with lower bound > 0: FAILED; otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED

H10.question: Does regime-conditioned calibration transfer outside its fitting regime?
H10.estimator: objective(regime model on the other regime's blocks) - objective(global v3 on the same blocks)
H10.threshold: noninferiority: Bonferroni upper bound < delta in both directions, delta = 0.10 x global model's selection objective (sealed)
H10.failure_semantics: a direction with lower bound > delta: FAILED; otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED

H11.question: Do ensemble-trained policies have more stable simulator-to-history conclusions than single-simulator-trained policies?
H11.estimator: per algorithm and fill mode: |historical - simulated| (policy - TWAP) mean cost difference for the ensemble variant minus the same for the single variant
H11.uncertainty: episode bootstrap of history with independent seed bootstrap of predictions, 5000 resamples
H11.threshold: per algorithm: Bonferroni upper bound < 0 under both fill modes
H11.failure_semantics: lower bound > 0 under both modes: FAILED; one mode only: ASSUMPTION_DEPENDENT; otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED
H11.status_rule: per algorithm ESTABLISHED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / FAILED / ASSUMPTION_DEPENDENT

H12.question: Are historical bounded-transfer conclusions stable under conservative and optimistic fill semantics?
H12.estimator: per agent pair: paired mean episode cost difference under each fill mode
H12.threshold: no pair has determinate opposite directions across modes and every determinate pair is determinate in both modes
H12.failure_semantics: any opposite-direction pair: FAILED; some pair determinate in one mode only: NOT_ESTABLISHED (those pairs ASSUMPTION_DEPENDENT)

F3_equifinality.size: sealed: 4 classical agents x C(K, 2) member pairs, K = ensemble size

F4_rank_stability.size: sealed: 15 agent pairs x K members

F10_scorecard_equivalence.scope: per dataset and model: one one-sided test per family against its sealed margin

bootstrap.moving_block: historical 600 s blocks (5-minute blocks for regime analyses) resampled with replacement
bootstrap.stationary: Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap available for sensitivity (mean block 600 s); not the primary method
bootstrap.paired: the same historical resample is applied to both models of a contrast
bootstrap.iid_rule: no IID bootstrap over dependent time-series samples; market seeds and episodes are independent units

statistics.equivalence: one-sided test of family error < sealed real-vs-real margin (the lower TOST bound is trivially satisfied because errors are nonnegative): EQUIVALENT_WITHIN_MARGIN if the one-sided upper bound < margin, FAILED_MARGIN if the lower bound > margin, NOT_EVALUABLE if missing, else NOT_ESTABLISHED
statistics.power: before holdout access: development/selection-based expected interval widths and minimum detectable effects for F1, F3, F4 and F8, sealed with the designs; an inconclusive result is never read as equivalence
statistics.invalid_cells: missing or INVALID planned cells withhold their comparison, count as not passing and never shrink a family

seeds.rule: every stochastic workflow takes its seed from this table or from a sealed design; no global random state

compute_budget.note: Budgets are fixed before evaluation. Reduced runs are labelled pilot and never presented as registered evidence.

accepted_reasons: holdout download failure after one retry (NOT_AVAILABLE)
source integrity failure: gzip/CRC, incomplete L2 replay, changed source bytes (INVALID)
more than 5% INVALID episodes in a world/agent cell (cell INVALID)
implementation bug discovered after a registered run (attempt retained as INVALID or FAILED; rerun after inspected outcomes is EXPLORATORY)
invalidation.retention: every attempt directory is kept and recorded by an 'attempt' ledger event; nothing is overwritten or deleted
invalidation.implementation_revisions: a fix after registration is sealed as '<analysis>-implementation-revision-N' with old and new source hashes before the rerun

exclusions: No live profitability, alpha, production trading, HFT, colocation, causal real-market, exact-FIFO, exact historical passive fill, hidden liquidity or universal cross-market claim follows from any v0.6 result.
Matching observed statistics does not prove that simulator mechanisms are correct.
Synthetic perturbation results describe the simulator only.
